absent: Locking discipline for topology masks, Hyper-V globals, MTRR caches and cleanup tables is not shown in these fragments.
Callers, ordering and concurrency context for the pairwise match helpers and the mask linker are not shown.
Meanings of individual Hyper-V feature, hint, privilege and isolation bits and full MSR and CPUID layouts are not shown.
MTRR cleanup search algorithm, trimming trigger conditions and memory map update failure handling beyond the single range update call are not shown.
Error paths and recovery for NMI registration, vector installation, clocksource setup and SMP hook selection are not shown.

findings.text: A small helper links two processors symmetrically in topology masks. Given an accessor that yields a mask for a processor plus two processor numbers, it records each number in the mask belonging to the other.

Sibling validation requires both processors to live on the same memory node. On mismatch it emits a one time warning naming both processors, the caller supplied relationship, and both node numbers, then reports failure; otherwise it reports success.

Thread sibling matching has two modes. With extended topology present it requires equal package, die, AMD node and cache identifiers, then accepts either equal core identifiers or equal non default compute unit identifiers, each gated by same node validation. Without extended topology it requires equal package, die and core identifiers gated by same node validation.

Die matching first requires equal package and die identifiers. When extended topology is enabled and more than one AMD node per package exists it also requires equal AMD node identifiers; otherwise package plus die equality alone accepts.

Second level cache matching falls back to thread sibling matching when the first processor lacks a valid second level identifier. Otherwise it rejects on identifier mismatch and otherwise delegates to same node validation under the cache relationship.
Package matching accepts exactly when both processors carry the same package identifier.

Last level cache matching rejects when the first processor has an invalid identifier or when the two identifiers differ. With cache splitting configured it also rejects when core numbers disagree modulo the split factor. A processor match table detects a sub NUMA mode where same package but different node quietly rejects to expose separate caches. Remaining equal cache pairs are gated by same node validation.
Reduced hardware early setup neutralizes timer bring up and pre vector interrupt setup by pointing both hooks at a no operation routine.

Hypervisor version query first reads the maximum supported leaf and fails as device not present with a diagnostic when the version leaf lies beyond that limit. Otherwise it fills the caller supplied version structure from the version leaf and reports success.
Hyper-V debug fast fail vector number is decimal 41, hexadecimal 0x29.
Hyper-V debug assert vector number is decimal 44, hexadecimal 0x2C.
Hyper-V debug service vector number is decimal 45, hexadecimal 0x2D.
NT asynchronous procedure call vector number is decimal 31, hexadecimal 0x1F.
NT deferred procedure call vector number is decimal 47, hexadecimal 0x2F.
NT clock inter processor interrupt vector number is decimal 210, hexadecimal 0xD2.

Root vector reservation marks six debug and NT vectors as allocated in the global system vector bitmap and announces them. It skips entirely on flexible return systems and halts on any double reservation, treating collision as unrecoverable.

Hyper-V platform bring up proceeds from discovery to tuning to device setup. Discovery records the hypervisor name, samples feature and limit leaves, identifies partition type, reserves root vectors, adjusts hints for secure interrupt delivery and nested execution, and samples virtual stack properties for confidential channel and extended destination support.

When frequency registers are advertised the platform adopts Hyper-V calibration for TSC and processor clocks and forces a known frequency capability. When isolation is advertised it samples isolation configuration, derives a shared boundary from a bit count when active, then selects SNP versus TDX behavior with matching static keys and hypercall pages, and for TDX without paravisor drops several hints, forces reduced hardware setup, and warns when invariant TSC is absent.

Late Hyper-V setup samples nested features when available, derives the local APIC timer period from the Hyper-V frequency register when supported, registers an unknown NMI handler, disables timer probing on IO APIC builds, installs power and crash handlers by root versus guest role, exposes invariant TSC when advertised, overrides NMI reason under EFI boot, then hooks post APIC init, installs callback and timer vectors, selects SMP hooks, forces physical x2APIC destination, initializes clocks, marks TSC unstable for non root guests without invariant TSC, and disables the hard lockup detector.
The x2APIC availability query reports whether the underlying x2APIC support test succeeds.
The MSI extended destination query returns the flag cached from virtual stack properties during platform initialization.

Secure encrypted virtualization hypercall preparation copies three general registers from the trap frame into the guest host communication block while return address and privilege state stay already present; completion needs no return state check and always reports success.

The Microsoft Hyper-V descriptor carries a name, detection and type fields, x2APIC availability, MSI destination, platform init and late guest init hooks, plus secure encrypted virtualization prepare and finish hooks when AMD memory encryption is configured.

K6 range read selects one of two packed regions from one register, upper half for region one and lower half for region zero. Base comes from high address bits at page granularity. Low bits select uncacheable versus write combining, with both clear meaning disabled and zero size. Otherwise size derives from an inverted coarse mask with a small bias.

K6 range write preserves both packed halves, clears the selected half when size is zero, otherwise encodes base plus inverted size mask plus type biased low bits with two complement arithmetic, flushes caches with write back invalidate, then writes the combined value back to the same register.

K6 addition validation accepts only uncacheable or write combining types, sizes of at least 128 kilobytes that are a power of two, and bases aligned to the size; anything else fails as invalid argument.
The AMD K6 operations table advertises two variable registers and binds set, get, generic free region search, K6 validation, and an affirmative write combining probe.

Centaur state keeps eight cached entries each with separate high and low halves, a reserved bitmask that allocation must skip, and a chip type flag distinguishing original WinChip from WinChip2 behavior.

Centaur free region search honors an explicit replacement index inside the variable range count, otherwise scans in order skipping reserved entries and returns the first entry whose size reads as zero, or reports no space when none qualifies.

Centaur range read derives base from the cached high half and size from the negated page aligned low half. Default type is write combining, refined by low control bits differently for the two chip generations to also report uncacheable or write back.

Centaur range write encodes disable as zero, otherwise places base in the high half and negated size plus control bits in the low half, using a fixed combining pattern on the older generation and a type selected pattern on the newer generation, then caches both halves and writes them to the per register address.
Centaur addition validation requires write combining on the older generation and additionally allows uncacheable on the newer generation, warning and rejecting as invalid argument otherwise.
The Centaur operations table advertises eight variable registers and binds Centaur set, get, free region search, validation, and an affirmative write combining probe.

Cleanup bookkeeping defines a range descriptor with base page number, size in pages and memory type, plus a tuning descriptor with start, size, chunk and granularity in kilobytes and a register index.
Cleanup result records granularity, chunk size and lost coverage in kilobytes together with a register count and a badness flag.
Maximum cleanup range count is 256 entries.
Cleanup keeps a fixed boot time array of address ranges with a live count plus a parallel array of variable range states.
A variable register holding unexpected uncacheable coverage below one megabyte is treated as a firmware defect and reported with a dedicated warning naming the register.
MTRR cleanup defaults from build configuration and is forced off by one boot option handler and forced on by another, each consuming its option string and reporting success.

Cleanup tuning defaults chunk size to 256 megabytes, granularity to zero, and spare register count from build configuration. Each has a boot option parser that rejects a missing argument and otherwise decodes a size or integer value and reports success.
Cleanup keeps 136 result slots.
Cleanup page to kilobyte shift equals page shift less ten.
Cleanup keeps a boot time result table sized by the result count and a parallel minimum loss table sized by the range count, plus a running range sum accumulator.
Memory trimming defaults to enabled and is permanently disabled by a boot option handler that sets the flag and reports success.
Top of memory two enabled flag is bit 21.
Top of memory two force write back flag is bit 22.

Memory trimming converts start and limit page numbers to byte addresses, derives length as their difference, and reclassifies that span from usable memory to reserved in the memory map, propagating the update result.
Version query helper is globally visible so other boot and guest code can sample the hypervisor version structure.
Hypervisor descriptor is globally visible constant data publishing Hyper-V detection and operations to generic selection.
AMD and Centaur operation tables are globally visible constant data publishing vendor range handling to generic selection.
